newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDESpar to sell Petrobras preference shrs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDESpar to sell Petrobras preference shrs.

text.p: The investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank, BNDESpar, is planning to auction off preference shares in state oil giant Petrobras held in its portfolio worth $510 million in total.
BNDESpar Director Nelson Rosental said BNDESpar was hoping to auction off an initial block of shares worth $110 million on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange May 23.

The remaining $400 million will be sold off in a global offer tentatively scheduled for July, with $300 million worth of shares being sold abroad and $100 million worth of shares going on offer in Brazil.
Credit Suisse First Boston is coordinating the global offer, while Itau Bankers Trust and Bozano Simonsen are in charge of the Brazilian sell-off, Rosental said.
He said the tender document for the May 23 auction was expected to be published Wednesday.
The minimum price for the preference shares on offer May 23 will be set according to a complicated calculation method.

A "basic price" will be set by picking the higher of two values, either 220 reais per lot of 1,000 shares or the average Petrobras share price on the stock exchange in the 20 days immediately prior to the publication of the tender document, Rosental said.
On the day of the auction, the minimum price will be set by comparing the basic price with the average price of Petrobras shares during morning trade.

If the average trading price is equal or higher than the basic price the auction will take place, setting the trading price as the minimum price. If the average trading price is lower than the basic price then the auction will be postponed until the next day, Rosental said.

He said the sell-off was "guaranteed" by 32 financial institutions which had committed themselves to buying specific share amounts each at the minimum price if no other buyers participated in the sell-off.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
